finding.claim: dropTable never enforces its 'dba' role check: the Authorize error is discarded, so any caller who reaches /admin/drop executes the DROP regardless of role.
finding.source: Any HTTP request to /admin/drop from a caller whose context has a *User (roles are irrelevant to the outcome).
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27, a destructive DDL operation gated by the dba role.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered to dropTable with no middleware in this file.
u := userFrom(r) loads the user from request context.
Authorize(u, "dba") returns an error for non-dba users, but the return value is ignored (contrast vacuum at lines 33-36, which checks it).
Execution continues unconditionally to runSQL with the attacker-supplied table name.
Returns 204 No Content, so the bypass succeeds silently.

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) computes the correct result but it is discarded. No route middleware is visible in api.go. Upstream authentication that populates the context user was not in the repo, so whether unauthenticated callers can reach this handler is unknown. Any authenticated user with any role can do this, which grants more than the dba role holds, so it is reportable.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. api.go:13-20 (Authorize) returns an error for non-dba users, but api.go:26 calls it as a bare statement and discards the result. api.go:44 registers /admin/drop with no middleware. Contrast api.go:33-36 in vacuum, which checks the error. runSQL at api.go:27 receives the raw r.FormValue("t") concatenated into the statement.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: userFrom at api.go:25, the discarded Authorize call at api.go:26, the unconditional DROP at api.go:27, and the route at api.go:44. Any caller whose request context holds a *User (api.go:22, which panics for anonymous requests rather than running the DROP) can run the DROP regardless of role, so the dba check is bypassed. The only open point is upstream authentication, which is not in this repo; it does not block the bypass for any authenticated low-privilege user.

finding.claim: The 't' form value is concatenated directly into a DROP TABLE statement with no identifier allowlist or quoting, allowing SQL injection (and stacked statements, depending on the driver).
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (query string or form body, any HTTP method).

trace.note: Route /admin/drop is publicly registered to dropTable.
r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into the DDL string with no validation.

finding.guards_checked: No validation, escaping, or allowlist on t. Identifiers cannot be parameterized, so an allowlist is required. The dba check is also absent (see AUTHZ-1), so the precondition is only reaching the handler. runSQL is a stub in this repo, so impact is judged from its semantics as a SQL executor.

verdict.guard_found: No effective guard on the concatenation at api.go:27. Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 returns an error that is discarded as a bare statement, so it blocks nothing. userFrom at api.go:22 only type-asserts the context user and panics if it is missing, which is a crash, not an access control. No allowlist, quoting, or parameterization of t exists.
verdict.reason: The trace's step "runSQL executes the resulting string" is wrong: runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub (`func runSQL(string) {}`), so in this repo nothing is executed and the injection cannot be shown to have an effect. The concatenation at api.go:27 and the discarded Authorize at api.go:26 are real and would be a serious flaw if runSQL were a real executor, but the finding as stated (SQL injection with execution) is not supported by this code, and the route at api.go:44 has no auth middleware in this repo, so the attacker tier is also unverifiable.
